title: bug: report_blocked by a governor on an unassigned task returns an END_SESSION handoff addressed to the governor, so the account-switch mod ends the governor's TUI session
description:
Observed 2026-10-31 02:12Z, filed by governor-4764040b.

What happened: governor-4764040b parked the unassigned CQ-R13 f4811a72 with moe.report_blocked, as a third party.
- The reply carried `sessionHandoff {action:'END_SESSION', workerId:'governor-4764040b'}`, plus seatFreed:true and workerStatus:'IDLE'.
- The governor holds no task, yet the moe-account-switch mod in its interactive TUI (scripts/mods/moe-account-switch/hooks/register.ts endSessionInstruction) latches any top-level END_SESSION addressed to its worker id.
- The mod then refuses chat_wait and runs /exit after the turn. The governance loop dies mid-incident, and the wrapper relaunches a fresh session that has lost its context.

Mechanism: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/reportBlocked.ts, around :481.
- `const seatWorker = prevAssignee || params.workerId;`. On an unassigned task the handoff falls back to the CALLER.
- `!currentTaskId` is then true for a governor, which never holds a task.

Constraint: keep the case the fallback exists for. That is a worker whose own launched task lost its assignment and that then reports the block; its session must still end.

Fix is the planner's call. For example: no fallback when the caller is a governor or human, or when the caller never held the task.
definitionOfDone: Daemon regression test, RED on the parent: report_blocked on an unassigned task by a governor-role caller returns no sessionHandoff, and leaves the governor's worker status unchanged.
The assignee's own report_blocked and the dropped-assignment worker case still return END_SESSION addressed to that worker.

implementationPlan.description:
RED: add the regression rows to packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/reportBlocked.test.ts, in the first describe block, right after the test 'reports the caller seat status honestly when a non-assignee updates an unassigned BLOCKED row'. Reuse its helpers (report, addWorker); change no existing test. A verified prototype (+35 lines) is in Serena memory `task-task-b60cb68c4ae74ffda43e617c7466911e-handoff`.

(1) Governor rows, it.each (DoD 1). For each row, set task-1 to assignedWorkerId null (WORKING), register the caller with addWorker, then set its status:
- ['governor-1', no team, status 'GOVERNING']: the role comes from the id prefix only.
- ['ops-seat', team role 'governor', status 'IDLE']: the role comes from the team only. The status is not GOVERNING, so a status-based fix fails this row.
Call report({ workerId: <governor>, reason: 'parked by governance' }) and assert:
- result.sessionHandoff toBeUndefined();
- result.workerStatus === the row's status. This is the honest reply; the parent answered a phantom 'IDLE'.
- the task is { status:'BLOCKED', assignedWorkerId:null, blockedReason:'parked by governance' }, so the park still happens;
- the stored worker is { status:<row status>, currentTaskId:null }, unchanged.

(2) Dropped-assignment rows, it.each (DoD 2: the case the caller fallback exists for). Use [worker-1/worker/WORKING], [qa-1/qa/REVIEW] and [architect-1/architect/PLANNING]: a seat whose own task lost its assignment before it reported, as with a governor release_task, a status move, or the REVIEW stale release. For each row, set task-1 to { status, assignedWorkerId:null } and register the caller (worker-1 already exists). Call report({ workerId: caller }) and assert:
- sessionHandoff toMatchObject { action:'END_SESSION', taskId:'task-1', workerId: caller };
- the task is BLOCKED and unassigned, with blockedFromStatus = status.

The existing test 'ends a freed-seat session instead of directing an in-CLI cross-task claim' keeps covering the assignee's own report (END_SESSION to worker-1); leave it unchanged.

RED evidence: run the step-3 snapshot recipe with ONLY this test file overlaid (the parent reportBlocked.ts) and `npx vitest run src/tools/reportBlocked.test.ts`. Expected, and seen in planning: exactly the 2 governor rows fail, with `expected { action: 'END_SESSION', … } to be undefined`, and the other 59 pass. Name them in the step note.
implementationPlan.note: RED in snapshot (test overlay only, parent reportBlocked.ts): 2 failed / 59 passed — 'a governor (governor-1, team role null)…' and 'a governor (ops-seat, team role governor)…', both 'expected { action: END_SESSION } to be undefined'. Shared checkout dirty paths (12, other sessions) untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN: three small edits in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/reportBlocked.ts, nothing else.

(a) The handoff target, around :479. Import resolveWorkerRole from '../util/workerRole.js' (team role wins, else the id prefix; the same helper claim_next_task uses to redirect governors). Then replace `const seatWorker = prevAssignee || params.workerId;` with:

    const callerSeat = params.workerId && resolveWorkerRole(state, params.workerId) !== 'governor'
      ? params.workerId : undefined;
    const seatWorker = prevAssignee || callerSeat;

Above it, add a comment of at most 3 lines: the caller fallback is for a seat whose own task lost its assignment before it reported; a governor never holds a task, so its third-party park must not end the governance session.

(b) The reply's workerStatus, around :552. Change `freeSeat ? (prevAssignee ? state.getWorker(prevAssignee)?.status ?? 'IDLE' : 'IDLE') : …` to `freeSeat && prevAssignee ? state.getWorker(prevAssignee)?.status ?? 'IDLE' : …`. An unassigned park then falls through to the existing arms, which report the caller's own real status (else 'IDLE' with no workerId), exactly as the comment above it already promises. The literal 'IDLE' was the same phantom that comment forbids.

(c) The tool description. Extend the parenthetical '(a third-party/workerId-less block on an assigned task keeps the hold' with '; a governor parking an unassigned task keeps its own session and status)'. The text 'End the current session' must stay (a test pins it).

Unchanged on purpose:
- freeSeat and seatFreed: test :1184 pins seatFreed:true for a workerId-less unassigned park.
- every write path.
- the other END_SESSION emitters (util/claimEligibility.ts, util/teamMembershipHeal.ts).
- scripts/mods/moe-account-switch. Its latch is right for a message really addressed to its seat (governor ruling, 02:16Z).
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md: four open WORKING rows declare it. Name the stale wording at lines 1203 and 1255 as a follow-up in the completion summary.

Error handling: resolveWorkerRole never throws. An unknown or unregistered id resolves to null and keeps today's fallback; a workerId-less call still gets no handoff. Nothing new is written, so a failure cannot leave partial state.

GREEN: the full test file passes (61 tests in planning), and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN in snapshot: tsc clean, reportBlocked.test.ts 61/61. Three edits only: import, callerSeat guard, workerStatus arm, description clause.

- Is the reply change additive and non-breaking (epic rail: no breaking MCP contract changes)? sessionHandoff stays optional and workerStatus keeps its value domain.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.report_blocked on an unassigned PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW task called by a governor-role seat parks the task exactly as before. It returns no sessionHandoff, and the reply's workerStatus is the governor's real stored status, which the call never changes. Every other caller keeps today's handoff: the assignee's own report, and a non-governor seat whose own task lost its assignment, still get END_SESSION addressed to that seat when it holds no other task.
acceptanceCriteria: Governor by id prefix (governor-1, GOVERNING) and governor by team role only (ops-seat, IDLE): sessionHandoff undefined, workerStatus equals the stored status, task BLOCKED and unassigned, worker record unchanged. These rows fail on the parent.
Dropped-assignment worker/WORKING, qa/REVIEW and architect/PLANNING callers on an unassigned task: END_SESSION addressed to the caller.
The assignee's own non-resource report: END_SESSION to the assignee (existing test unchanged).
invariants: No write path changes: the task flip, assignment clearing, worker touches, chat posts and attempt handling are byte-identical in effect.
freeSeat and seatFreed semantics are unchanged (test :1184 still passes).
The handoff is never addressed to a seat that holds another task (the existing currentTaskId guard).
Existing tests in reportBlocked.test.ts are unedited and green.
compatibility: MCP contract: sessionHandoff stays optional and workerStatus keeps its value domain. Additive and non-breaking (epic rail).
Existing .moe state needs no migration; role resolution reads teams and ids only.

reportBlocked.test.ts: 2 governor rows and 3 dropped-assignment rows.

The existing report and addWorker test helpers.

reportBlocked.ts:479-489 seatWorker = prevAssignee || params.workerId; END_SESSION when freeSeat && seatWorker && !currentTaskId.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) Exempt callers that never held the task, using attempt history: rejected. It also covers idle architect or QA third-party parks, but it fails open for the real dropped-assignment seat whenever attempt records are missing (legacy rows, heals, pruned attempts). That seat would then keep its session and could claim another task in-session, the defect 43f6dd55 fixed. Ending a session wrongly is recoverable; a cross-task claim inside one session corrupts landing attribution. (b) Change the mod: ruled out by the governor (02:16Z). (c) Change freeSeat or seatFreed for unassigned rows: broader, and it breaks the pinned test :1184. (d) Role-based governor exemption: chosen. A governor can never be the dropped-assignment seat, so it is exact for the reported defect, and it is the DoD's wording.
